neutral_facts.value: The accused, a government servant working as a watchman, assaulted his wife and mother with a sharp edged weapon, causing the death of his 1.5-year-old daughter. The victim's cries after the assault attracted the accused's attention, leading to her injury. The accused confined the victims inside the house and was later found with the weapon. The prosecution case established that the accused assaulted his wife and mother, leading to the daughter's death. The accused's conduct was scrutinized for premeditation, but the evidence suggested it was a sudden quarrel and heat of passion. The accused was initially convicted of murder, but the conviction was modified to culpable homicide not amounting to murder due to lack of premeditation.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The Supreme Court accepted the prosecution's case that the appellant assaulted his wife and mother with a sharp edged weapon, caused the death of his daughter, and wrongfully confined his wife and mother within the house. The court also accepted the evidence of the injuries sustained by the wife and mother, the post-mortem report of the daughter, and the testimonies of the medical experts.

quotes.text: The deposition of PW2, the wife of the appellant completely supported the prosecution case and the sequence of events leading to the heartless killing of the innocent child 'A'

witness_credibility.value: The court assessed the main witnesses, particularly PW2 (the wife), as credible and reliable, noting that she not only suffered the assault but survived to provide detailed accounts. The court also found PW1 and PW8 to be supportive of PW2's version. PW3's credibility was undermined due to her hostile testimony and attempt to attribute her injuries to a fall.

quotes.text: There is no reason whatsoever to disbelieve the deposition of PW2 who unlike 'A' not only suffered the murderous assault but survived to tell the tale in all its details that leave no room for any doubt about her version being completely reliable

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant picked up a quarrel with his wife, assaulted her with a sharp edged weapon, and when his mother intervened to save his wife, she too was assaulted. The ruckus caused by the quarrel and assault woke up the 1 1/2 year old daughter, who started crying, and the appellant went inside the room and hit her, causing her death. The appellant then wrongfully confined his wife and mother within the house.

quotes.text: The prosecution case was that the appellant picked up a quarrel with his wife (PW2) and thereafter assaulted her with a sharp edged weapon and when PW3, the mother of appellant, intervened to save PW2, she too was assaulted by the appellant and resultantly both PWs 2 and 3 were rendered injured

defence_argument.value: The appellant's counsel argued that the material on record sufficiently proved that he was a person of unsound mind, that he had been treated by a Psychiatrist and was taking medicines for his illness, that the writings on the walls of the appellant's house suggested he was mentally unsound, and that his conduct after the event was suggestive of his being of unsound mind.

quotes.text: The appellant's conduct after the event was also argued to be suggestive of his being of unsound mind, which aspects, it was contended that the courts below had failed to appreciate in the process denying to the appellant the benefit of Section 84 .of IPC, legitimately due to him.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Court applied the principle that the burden of proving the existence of circumstances that would bring the case within the purview of Section 84 of the IPC lies squarely upon the person claiming the benefit of that provision. The standard of proof for discharge of the burden is not the same as that expected of the prosecution.

quotes.text: The burden of bringing his/her case under Section 84 of the IPC lies squarely upon the person claiming the benefit of that provision. Section 105 of the Evidence Act is in this regard relevant.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed based on the finding that the appellant committed culpable homicide without premeditation in a sudden fight and in the heat of passion. The Court held that the appellant did not act in a cruel or unusual manner and did not take an undue advantage. The conviction under Section 302 was not justified, and the sentence was modified to Section 304 Part-II with 10 years rigorous imprisonment.

quotes.text: The appellant committed culpable homicide without premeditation in a sudden fight and in the heat of passion. The fact that the appellant did not use the sharp edged weapon with which he was armed also shows that he did not act in a cruel or unusual manner nor did he take an undue advantage.

judicial_mitigating_factors.value: The Court considered that the appellant was working as a government servant with no history of mental health complaints, and that his wife and mother did not suggest any mental ailment except for sleeplessness, which was attributed to excessive drinking.

quotes.text: The fact that the appellant was working as a government servant and was posted as a Watchman with no history of any complaint as to his mental health from anyone supervising his duties, is significant.

judicial_aggravating_factors.value: The Court considered that the appellant assaulted his wife, mother, and child, and that the assault on the child resulted in fatal injuries, indicating a lack of understanding of the consequences of his actions.

quotes.text: The Court considered that the appellant assaulted his wife, mother, and child, and that the assault on the child resulted in fatal injuries, indicating a lack of understanding of the consequences of his actions.
